analysis.note: Locative singular of the whole compound. The commentary expands it as the vaiśāradya of nirvicāra samādhi and uses it conditionally: yadā ... tadā ....

verification.detail: compound stem nirvicāravaiśāradya as Napumsaka/Saptami/Eka: pass; relation tatpurusa: unsupported (logged)

analysis.note: Nominative singular predicate with an ellipsed bhavati supplied by the commentary. Rendered as inner clarity, not divine favor/grace.

verification.detail: compound stem adhyātmaprasāda as Pum/Prathama/Eka: pass; relation tatpurusa: unsupported (logged)

justifications.decision: The word vaiśāradya is rendered by “lucidity” because Vyāsa defines it as an unoverpowered, transparent, steady flow of the luminous buddhisattva after impurity and covering have been removed.
justifications.chosen: vaiśāradya as lucid clearness/settled transparency of the cognitive sattva, not merely practical skill or expertise

evidence.quote: aśuddhyāvaraṇamalāpetasya prakāśātmano buddhisattvasya rajastamobhyām anabhibhūtaḥ svacchaḥ sthitipravāho vaiśāradyam.
evidence.translation: Vaiśāradya is the transparent steady-flow of the luminous buddhisattva, free from the impurity-covering stain and not overpowered by rajas and tamas.

justifications.decision: The compound is construed as a genitive tatpuruṣa, with nirvicāra qualifying samādhi; the sūtra’s locative is temporal/conditional, not simply a static location.
options_considered: conditional/temporal locative: when lucidity of nirvicāra samādhi arises
locative of sphere: in expertise concerning nirvicāra
adjectival reading: in a clear state needing no consideration
justifications.chosen: nirvicāravaiśāradye = ‘when lucidity in/of the nirvicāra samādhi has arisen’

evidence.quote: yadā nirvicārasya samādher vaiśāradyam idaṃ jāyate tadā
evidence.translation: When this vaiśāradya of the nirvicāra samādhi arises, then ...

justifications.decision: The second compound is not taken as ‘grace of the Supreme Spirit’ or external favor. Vyāsa says it comes to the yogin and qualifies it by its real-object scope and clarity.
justifications.chosen: adhyātmaprasādaḥ as the yogin’s inner clarity, a clear cognition concerning things as they are

evidence.quote: tadā yogino bhavaty adhyātmaprasādo bhūtārthaviṣayaḥ kramānanurodhī sphuṭaḥ
evidence.translation: Then the yogin has adhyātmaprasāda, whose object is the real thing, not dependent on sequence, distinct/clear.

justifications.decision: The sūtra has no finite verb; the commentary supplies jāyate for the condition and bhavati for the result, so the translation uses ‘has arisen ... comes to the yogin.’
options_considered: elliptic existential/result clause: inner clarity comes to be
justifications.chosen: supply the finite sense as ‘comes to be/arises’

evidence.translation: [It] arises; then adhyātmaprasāda comes to be for the yogin.

translation: When lucidity (vaiśāradya) has arisen in the nirvicāra samādhi, inner clarity (adhyātma-prasāda) comes to the yogin.
one_shot_delta: A commentary-blind translation might render vaiśāradya as ordinary “expertise/skill,” but Vyāsa defines it as transparent, steady lucidity of buddhisattva.
It might take adhyātmaprasāda as “grace of the Supreme Spirit,” using possible dictionary senses, whereas the bhāṣya treats it as the yogin’s clear cognition concerning real objects.
It might fail to supply samādhi after nirvicāra and miss the yadā–tadā conditional structure: when that lucidity arises, then inner clarity comes to be.
open_questions: Commentary line 2 ends with the incomplete-looking string “praj”; this apparatus does not rely on any unprovided completion.
